answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring staked identity beacons: each agent posts a collateral bond before its beacon announcement is accepted, and peer nodes rate-limit new arrivals the way a desert oasis rations water. Every fresh identity must lock real funds and wait through a probation period - costly, like seasoning timber before construction - so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents burns capital per persona. Slashable bonds make mass impersonation uneconomical: a caught cheater forfeits the stake that vouched for it.
